which-system.statement: The new State Pension is for men born on or after 6 April 1951 and women born on or after 6 April 1953. People born before those dates are on the basic State Pension.
which-system.passage: a man born on or after 6 April 1951 ... a woman born on or after 6 April 1953

starting-amount.statement: For a National Insurance record that began before April 2016, a starting amount was worked out. It can be less than, more than or equal to the full rate.
starting-amount.passage: Your 'starting amount' could be less than, more than or equal to the full new State Pension.

contracted-out.statement: People who were contracted out usually need more than 35 qualifying years for the full rate.
contracted-out.passage: If you were contracted out, you will usually need more than 35 qualifying years to get the full rate of new State Pension.

ni-credits.statement: National Insurance credits can fill gaps in a record, for example during unemployment, illness or caring.
ni-credits.passage: Credits can help to fill gaps in your National Insurance record, to make sure you qualify for certain benefits including the State Pension.

spa-67.statement: State Pension age is rising from 66 to 67 between 2026 and 2028.
spa-67.passage: The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028.

spa-68.statement: The law provides for a rise from 67 to 68 between 2044 and 2046. A review could change that timetable.
spa-68.passage: Under the Pensions Act 2007 the State Pension age for men and women will increase from 67 to 68 between 2044 and 2046.

spa-review.statement: A third review of State Pension age was launched in July 2025. No report from it was listed on GOV.UK when this site was checked.
spa-review.passage: The government announced the launch of the third review of State Pension age in July 2025.
spa-review.note: The absence of a report was checked on the GOV.UK collection page only.

claim-not-automatic.statement: The State Pension is not paid automatically. It has to be claimed.
claim-not-automatic.passage: You will not get your new State Pension automatically - you have to claim it.

deferral-default.statement: A State Pension that is not claimed at State Pension age is deferred.
deferral-default.passage: If you do not claim your State Pension at State Pension age, it automatically defers.

protected-payment-cpi.statement: A protected payment rises each year in line with the Consumer Prices Index, not the triple lock.
protected-payment-cpi.passage: If you have a protected payment, it increases each year in line with the CPI.

deferral-increase-cpi.statement: Extra pension earned by deferring usually rises with the Consumer Prices Index.
deferral-increase-cpi.passage: the extra amount you get because you deferred will usually increase each year based on the Consumer Price Index. It will not increase for some people who live abroad.

taxable-paid-gross.statement: The State Pension is taxable income, but no tax is taken off before it is paid.
taxable-paid-gross.passage: Your State Pension is taxable income, but tax is not taken off before you get it.

simple-assessment.statement: Where tax is due and cannot be collected another way, HM Revenue and Customs sends a Simple Assessment bill.
simple-assessment.passage: If you go over your Personal Allowance and you have tax to pay, HMRC will send you a Simple Assessment tax bill.

simple-assessment-2027.statement: The government has said that from 2027-28 pensioners whose only income is the basic or new State Pension, without increments, will not have to pay small amounts of tax through Simple Assessment. It has not published how. This is an announcement, not law.
simple-assessment-2027.passage: The government will ease the administrative burden for pensioners whose sole income is the basic or new State Pension without any increments so that they do not have to pay small amounts of tax via Simple Assessment from 2027-28

paid-four-weekly.statement: The State Pension is usually paid every 4 weeks.
paid-four-weekly.passage: The new State Pension is usually paid into your account every 4 weeks.

paid-in-arrears.statement: The new State Pension is paid in arrears, which means each payment covers the weeks just gone.
paid-in-arrears.passage: State pension is to be paid in arrears.

pay-as-you-go.statement: National Insurance is run on a pay-as-you-go basis: contributions paid this year meet the cost of benefits paid this year.
pay-as-you-go.passage: The National Insurance scheme is financed on a pay as you go basis with contribution rates set at a level broadly necessary to meet the expected benefits expenditure in that year

overseas-frozen.statement: People who live abroad get yearly increases only in the European Economic Area, Gibraltar, Switzerland and countries with an agreement that provides for them. Canada and New Zealand are excluded.
overseas-frozen.passage: countries that have a social security agreement with the UK (but you cannot get increases in Canada or New Zealand) ... You will not get yearly increases if you live outside these countries.

overseas-return.statement: The pension goes up to the current rate if the person returns to live in the UK.
overseas-return.passage: Your pension will go up to the current rate if you return to live in the UK.

housing-benefit.statement: A single person who has reached State Pension age can make a new claim for Housing Benefit. A couple normally can only if both have reached State Pension age. There are exceptions, for example for supported, sheltered or temporary housing.
housing-benefit.passage: You've reached State Pension age If you're single you can make a new claim for Housing Benefit. … you and your partner have both reached State Pension age … you're in supported, sheltered or temporary housing

pc-mixed-age.statement: A couple can normally get Pension Credit only if both have reached State Pension age, or one of them gets Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age.
pc-mixed-age.passage: You'll be eligible if either: you and your partner have both reached State Pension age … one of you is getting Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age … You will stop getting Pension Credit if you start living with a partner who is under State Pension age.

wfp-automatic.statement: Most people who are eligible get the Winter Fuel Payment automatically.
wfp-automatic.passage: Most people get the Winter Fuel Payment automatically if they're eligible.

care-means-test-allowances.statement: In England, the means test for council-funded care must leave a person enough income after housing costs and disability-related spending.
care-means-test-allowances.passage: This must be after any housing costs such as rent and council tax net of any benefits provided to support these costs – and after any disability related expenditure.
care-means-test-allowances.note: Annex C, paragraph 49, on the minimum income guarantee. Paragraph 39 says the council should allow for necessary disability-related expenditure.

council-tax-reduction.statement: Council Tax Reduction is run by local councils and the rules vary by area.
council-tax-reduction.passage: each council runs its own scheme

council-tax-reduction-pensioners.statement: In England, regulations prescribe classes of pensioners that each council's scheme has to include, so for pensioners the main rules are set nationally.
council-tax-reduction-pensioners.passage: the classes of pensioners described in paragraph 1 of Schedule 1 are classes of person prescribed
council-tax-reduction-pensioners.note: Regulation 11. The second half of the sentence is our reading of what that means for a pensioner.

ni-stops-at-spa.statement: Most people stop paying National Insurance when they reach State Pension age.
ni-stops-at-spa.passage: Most people stop paying National Insurance contributions after reaching State Pension age.

tl-definition.statement: The triple lock is a government commitment to raise the basic and new State Pension each year by the highest of earnings growth, price inflation or 2.5%.
tl-definition.passage: a government commitment to up-rate the basic and new State Pensions every year by the highest of earnings growth, inflation, or 2.5%

tl-policy-not-law.statement: The law requires an increase at least in line with earnings. The triple lock goes further and is a commitment, not a legal duty.
tl-policy-not-law.passage: The statutory minimum increase to the basic State Pension is the rise in earnings. The government has given a commitment to increase the basic State Pension in line with the Triple Lock

legal-earnings-floor.statement: Section 150A requires an increase of at least the percentage by which earnings have risen.
legal-earnings-floor.passage: increases each of the amounts referred to in subsection (1) above by a percentage not less than the percentage by which the general level of earnings is greater at the end of the period

earnings-measure-discretion.statement: The law leaves the choice of earnings measure to the Secretary of State.
earnings-measure-discretion.passage: the Secretary of State shall estimate the general level of earnings in such manner as he thinks fit

rounding-power.statement: The law allows the new amount to be rounded up or down.
rounding-power.passage: adjust the amount of the increase so as to round the sum in question up or down to such extent as he thinks appropriate

rounding-5p.statement: Full rates of the basic and new State Pension are rounded to the nearest 5p.
rounding-5p.passage: The majority of new rates are rounded to the nearest 5p. This includes, for example, the standard (full) rates of Category A and Category B basic State Pension and the full rate of new State Pension.
rounding-5p.note: The 2025 memorandum says 'rounded up to the nearest 5 pence', but the new State Pension that year was rounded down. Nearest-5p rounding reproduces every published full rate from 2010/11 to 2026/27.

no-order-if-earnings-fall.statement: If earnings do not rise, the ordinary law provides for no increase. It does not provide for a cut.
no-order-if-earnings-fall.passage: prevents the Secretary of State from bringing forward an Up-rating Order if earnings growth is negative.

tl-announced-2010.statement: The commitment was announced in May 2010 as a 'triple guarantee'.
tl-announced-2010.passage: restore the earnings link for the basic state pension from April 2011, with a 'triple guarantee' that pensions are raised by the higher of earnings, prices or 2.5%

tl-cpi-measure-2010.statement: The June 2010 Budget said the Consumer Prices Index would be the prices measure.
tl-cpi-measure-2010.passage: CPI will be used as the measure of prices in the triple guarantee

tl-2011-rpi.statement: In April 2011 the Retail Prices Index was used for the basic State Pension, for that year only.
tl-2011-rpi.passage: increased in line with the growth in the RPI for the 12 months to September 2010, which was 4.6%

tl-2021-act.statement: For April 2021, when earnings had fallen, a one-year Act allowed an increase of whatever percentage the Secretary of State thought fit.
tl-2021-act.passage: by such a percentage as the Secretary of State thinks fit

tl-2022-act.statement: For April 2022 a one-year Act replaced the earnings test with a prices test, with a minimum of 2.5%.

tl-2026-decision.statement: For April 2026 the increase was 4.8%, in line with earnings growth.
tl-2026-decision.passage: earnings over the relevant period (4.8%) is higher than ... the growth in prices (3.8%) and 2.5%

earnings-link-1980.statement: From 1980 the law required the yearly review to look only at prices.
earnings-link-1980.passage: the Secretary of State shall have regard only to prices

earnings-link-restored.statement: The law that restored the earnings link named 2010-11 as the first tax year in which rates are reviewed against earnings, so the first increase under it was in April 2011.
earnings-link-restored.passage: The designated tax year ... is the tax year 2010-11

tl-this-parliament.statement: The government's Budget documents commit to the triple lock for the length of this Parliament.
tl-this-parliament.passage: its commitment to the Triple Lock for the duration of this Parliament

tl-ratchet.statement: A year in which pay grows by less than prices, or less than 2.5%, lifts the pension permanently relative to earnings.
tl-ratchet.passage: any year in which nominal pay growth falls below the rate of inflation or below 2.5% will lead to a permanent upwards ratchet in the State Pension's value relative to earnings

tl-non-earnings-triggered.statement: The Office for Budget Responsibility counted, in July 2025, that the prices or 2.5% part of the lock had decided the increase in eight of the 13 years to that date.
tl-non-earnings-triggered.passage: the non-earnings elements of the lock triggered in eight of the 13 years to date
tl-non-earnings-triggered.note: The report does not list the years. The record on this site's history page gives a different count for some 13-year spans, depending on which years are counted and how April 2022 is treated.

mis-not-poverty-line.statement: The researchers say the Minimum Income Standard is not a poverty threshold.
mis-not-poverty-line.passage: MIS is relevant to the discussion of poverty, but it does not claim to be a poverty threshold.

mis-excludes-disability.statement: The Minimum Income Standard does not cover extra needs from disability or from living in a remote place.
mis-excludes-disability.passage: does not attempt to specify extra requirements for particular individuals and groups who may have additional needs, for example those resulting from living in a remote location or having a disability

mis-tenure-change.statement: In 2026 the budgets for pensioners assumed private renting for the first time. Before that they assumed social housing.
mis-tenure-change.passage: For the first time, MIS budgets for all household types now assume accommodation in the private rented sector.

mis-basket-change.statement: The researchers say changes to the basket generally mattered more than inflation for the 2026 budgets.
mis-basket-change.passage: in 2026 changes in the basket of goods and services ... have generally had a greater impact on what has happened to budgets overall than inflation.

mis-all-benefits-assumed.statement: The comparison of pension income with the budget assumes people receive every benefit they are entitled to.
mis-all-benefits-assumed.passage: assume that people are receiving all the benefits to which they are entitled

rls-after-tax.statement: The Retirement Living Standards are spending figures, so the income needed can be higher once tax is paid.
rls-after-tax.passage: To meet these costs, you'll need enough income after tax. This means the income you need may be higher than the figures shown.

rls-housing-assumption.statement: At the moderate and comfortable standards the research assumes people enter retirement with no mortgage or rent. At the minimum it assumes social housing.
rls-housing-assumption.passage: At both the moderate and comfortable living standards, groups have agreed that it remains a reasonable assumption that people at this level are entering retirement mortgage or rent free

fs-small-samples.statement: The Office for National Statistics warns that sample sizes remain small.
fs-small-samples.passage: While sample sizes increased in FYE 2025, they remain small, and users should be aware that estimates for lower-level expenditure categories in the underlying data are subject to greater uncertainty

hbai-owners.statement: Over three-quarters of pensioners live in homes owned outright, which is why fewer are in low income after housing costs than before.
hbai-owners.passage: Over three-quarters of pensioners live in homes that are owned outright
hbai-owners.note: The passage gives the share who own outright. The link to low income after housing costs is stated by the same publication in the sentence that follows it.

disability-income-artefact.statement: Low-income figures count disability benefits as income and make no allowance for the extra costs of disability, so they can understate hardship among disabled pensioners.
disability-income-artefact.passage: somewhat simplistic, adjusting income similarly for all people aged 14 and over in a household, regardless of whether the person is a child, working-age adult, pensioner, or disabled
disability-income-artefact.note: The second half of the statement is this site's reading of the publisher's caution about its method.

ifs-guarantee-1.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies recommends a target level for the new State Pension, set as a share of median full-time earnings, with increases that keep pace with earnings in the long run.
ifs-guarantee-1.passage: There will be a government target level for the new state pension, expressed as a share of median full-time earnings. Increases in the state pension will in the long run keep pace with growth in economy-wide average earnings

ifs-guarantee-2.statement: Under that proposal the pension would still rise at least in line with inflation every year.
ifs-guarantee-2.passage: Both before and after the target level is reached, the state pension will continue to increase at least in line with inflation every year.

ifs-guarantee-3.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies recommends that the State Pension is not means-tested.
ifs-guarantee-3.passage: The state pension will not be means-tested.

ifs-no-means-test-reason.statement: Its stated reason is that means-testing would discourage saving and could undermine automatic enrolment.
ifs-no-means-test-reason.passage: The temptation of an apparently lower-cost means-tested approach should be resisted as it would disincentivise saving for many and therefore risk undermining the success of automatic enrolment.

ifs-explicit-goal.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies argues that a government wanting a more generous pension should say so as a goal.
ifs-explicit-goal.passage: if the government wants a more generous state pension relative to average earnings then it would be better to set that as an explicit goal than to use the triple lock

ifs-not-immediately.statement: It says the triple lock would not have to end at once.
ifs-not-immediately.passage: under our guarantee the government would not have to move away from the triple lock immediately

ifs-range-2050.statement: Under the triple lock the value of the pension in 2050 is uncertain.
ifs-range-2050.passage: a reasonable range ... for the value of the new state pension in 2050 is between 31% and 37% of median full-time earnings

ifs-longevity.statement: People with a longer life expectancy gain relatively more from the triple lock.
ifs-longevity.passage: those with a higher life expectancy benefit relatively more from the triple lock, as they are more likely to be receiving a generously indexed state pension in their 90s and beyond

smoothed-link-definition.statement: Under a smoothed earnings link, the pension rises with prices when earnings growth is lower, until it is back at its target share of earnings.
smoothed-link-definition.passage: when average earnings growth is below the rate of inflation, the state pension should increase in line with inflation until the target level of the state pension is reached again

rf-smoothed-recommendation.statement: The Resolution Foundation recommends a smoothed earnings link.
rf-smoothed-recommendation.passage: The best option would be a 'smoothed' earnings link, which tracks earnings growth but protects the value of the State Pension from temporary price shocks.

rf-volatility.statement: The Resolution Foundation argues that generosity should not depend on how volatile the economy is.
rf-volatility.passage: It is impossible to justify why our generosity to the older population should be a function of economic volatility.

rf-living-standards.statement: The Resolution Foundation reports faster growth in living standards for pensioners than for others over two decades.
rf-living-standards.passage: Pensioners have seen three times as much living standards growth as non-pensioners over the last two decades

rf-poverty-since-2011.statement: It also reports that pensioner poverty has risen since 2011-12.
rf-poverty-since-2011.passage: since 2011-12, pensioner poverty has risen by 2.3 percentage points even with the triple lock in place

tbi-proposal.statement: The Tony Blair Institute proposes replacing the triple lock after 2030 with a smoothed earnings link, as part of a wider redesign.
tbi-proposal.passage: Replace the triple lock after 2030 with a smoothed earnings link. The triple lock has become a long-run cost escalator.

ppi-future-workers.statement: The Pensions Policy Institute notes the argument that the triple lock improves the pension even more for today's workers than for today's pensioners.
ppi-future-workers.passage: the triple lock actually improves the State Pension even more for the current workforce than for current pensioners

ppi-demographics.statement: The Pensions Policy Institute says the cost of an older population outweighs the cost of the triple lock.
ppi-demographics.passage: the increase in State Pension costs related to demographic changes significantly outweigh the increase in costs resulting from the triple lock
ppi-demographics.note: The Office for Budget Responsibility attributes 1.2% of GDP of a 3.6% rise to the triple lock. The two statements use different dates and baselines.

ppi-reliance.statement: Around 60% of pensioner households get most of their income from the state.
ppi-reliance.passage: Around 60% of pensioner households receive the majority of ... their income from the State, with State Pension making up 85% of that.

ageuk-largest-income.statement: Age UK says the State Pension is the largest single source of income for most pensioners.
ageuk-largest-income.passage: The State Pension is the largest single source of income for most pensioners.

ageuk-women.statement: Age UK reports higher poverty among women pensioners.
ageuk-women.passage: One in six pensioners live in relative poverty in the UK, and nearer to one in five women pensioners

pc-firm-foundation.statement: The Pensions Commission describes the State Pension as the foundation for retirement saving.
pc-firm-foundation.passage: The existing contributory non-means-tested State Pension is the firm foundation for retirement saving for the vast majority of the population.

pc-safety-net.statement: The Pensions Commission expects a means-tested safety net to remain necessary.
pc-safety-net.passage: A means-tested safety net will remain necessary but may need updating in light of rising numbers of pensioners renting privately.

pc-30-percent.statement: The Pensions Commission puts the full new State Pension at 30% of median earnings in 2025.
pc-30-percent.passage: the full rate of the new State Pension represented 30% of median earnings in 2025, up from 29% in 2016, almost achieving the 31% of median earnings envisaged by the first Commission

pc-terms.statement: The terms of reference of the Pensions Commission do not mention the triple lock or uprating by name.
pc-terms.passage: the role of private pension provision and wider savings, building on the foundation of the State Pension, in delivering financial security in retirement
pc-terms.note: The statement that the words do not appear is a reading of the whole document.

pc-final-2027.statement: The Pensions Commission plans its final report for spring 2027.
pc-final-2027.passage: Our final report is planned for Spring 2027.

wp-savings-credit.statement: A 2013 White Paper said Savings Credit had brought more pensioners into means-testing.
wp-savings-credit.passage: However, the Savings Credit has increased the number of pensioners within the scope of means-testing.

wp-above-means-test.statement: The new State Pension was set above the basic level of means-tested support.
wp-above-means-test.passage: The single-tier pension will be set at a rate that is above the basic level of means-tested support. As a result there will no longer be a need for a complex savings reward under single tier.

wp-beveridge.statement: The White Paper traces a contributory pension without a means test to the Beveridge report.
wp-beveridge.passage: Central to Beveridge's vision of a universal social insurance scheme was a basic non means-tested contributory retirement pension.

australia-assets-test.statement: Australia reduces its Age Pension where assets are above a limit.
australia-assets-test.passage: When your assets are more than the limit for your situation, your pension will reduce.
australia-assets-test.note: Context only. Australia's Age Pension is based on residence and paid from general taxation, and sits beside compulsory private saving. It is not a model proposed for the UK by any body we found.

no-costed-means-test.statement: We found no costed proposal from a party, commission or research body to means-test the UK State Pension.
no-costed-means-test.note: A finding of absence. The search covered the Office for Budget Responsibility, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, the Pensions Policy Institute, the Resolution Foundation and news reports, on 29 September 2026.

no-costed-double-lock.statement: We found no current official or research estimate, that we could open and check, of the saving from a double lock of prices or earnings.
no-costed-double-lock.note: A finding of absence. An Institute for Fiscal Studies article on the subject could not be opened. A figure of £2.6 billion attributed to the Social Market Foundation was seen in a news report only.

if-nic-proposal.statement: In a paper of 2018, the Intergenerational Foundation proposed National Insurance on the earnings of people over State Pension age.
if-nic-proposal.passage: At least £1.5 billion extra National Insurance revenue could be raised annually
if-nic-proposal.note: The date and price basis of the estimate were not confirmed.

double-lock-2017.statement: The Conservative manifesto of 2017 proposed a double lock from 2020. It was not introduced.
double-lock-2017.passage: we will keep our promise to maintain the Triple Lock until 2020, and when it expires we will introduce a new Double Lock, meaning that pensions will rise in line with the earnings that pay for them

obr-tl-assumed.statement: In its July 2026 report the Office for Budget Responsibility assumed the triple lock continues, because no firm alternative policy then existed.
obr-tl-assumed.passage: assume it remains in place beyond this point in the absence of a firm policy alternative

labour-manifesto-tl.statement: The Labour manifesto of 2024 promised to keep the triple lock.
labour-manifesto-tl.passage: Labour will retain the triple lock

conservative-position.statement: The Conservative leader was reported as saying the party stands by the triple lock.
conservative-position.passage: The Conservatives created the triple lock; we've always protected it and we stand by it.
conservative-position.note: Reported in a newspaper article of 19 September 2026, which dates the remark to September 2025. We found no party document.

libdem-position.statement: The Liberal Democrats say they support protecting the triple lock.
libdem-position.passage: We support protecting the triple lock so that pensions always rise in line with inflation, wages or 2.5% – whichever is highest.

reform-position.statement: Reform UK was reported as committing to keep the triple lock on 2 April 2026.
reform-position.note: Reported in a newspaper. We found no party document. No wording is quoted.

care-cap-cancelled.statement: The planned cap on care costs in England was cancelled on 29 July 2024.
care-cap-cancelled.passage: So it will not be possible to take forward these charging reforms. This will save over £1bn by the end of next year.

casey-first-terms.statement: The commission's published terms set two phases, the first reporting in 2026 and the second by 2028.
casey-first-terms.passage: The purpose of the first phase of the commission is to set out the plan for how to implement a national care service, a government manifesto commitment. This should report in 2026.

casey-tor-summer-2027.statement: On 1 October 2026 the government changed the terms to show a report in summer 2027.
casey-tor-summer-2027.passage: Updated the terms of reference for the Independent Commission on Adult Social Care to reflect the commission's revised timetable, including its new reporting date of summer 2027.

casey-tor-reinstated.statement: On the same day, 1 October 2026, the government put the original terms back and said an updated version would follow.
casey-tor-reinstated.passage: Reinstated the original version of the terms of reference, with an updated version to follow in due course.

casey-affordable.statement: The terms require recommendations to be affordable within spending plans for this Parliament.
casey-affordable.passage: The commission's recommendations must remain affordable, operating within the fiscal constraints of Spending Review settlements for the remainder of this Parliament.

casey-summer-2027.statement: On 29 July 2026 the Prime Minister's Office said the commission would report in summer 2027.
casey-summer-2027.passage: he would bring forward the date for Baroness Casey's commission to report back with a plan on how to deliver the National Care Service, accelerating this from 2028 to next summer

care-funded-principle.statement: On 29 July 2026 the Prime Minister's Office said the service must be fully funded. That announcement named no source of funding.
care-funded-principle.passage: This service must be fully and sustainably funded
care-funded-principle.note: That no funding source is named is a reading of the whole announcement.

casey-panel.statement: A public panel for the commission was opened for registration in September 2026.
casey-panel.passage: What is care? Who should receive it? And who should pay for what?

aa-scotland.statement: In Scotland, new claims are for Pension Age Disability Payment, not Attendance Allowance.
aa-scotland.passage: You will need to apply for Pension Age Disability Payment instead of Attendance Allowance.

aa-northern-ireland.statement: Attendance Allowance is also paid in Northern Ireland. Claim packs come from the Disability and Carers Service.
aa-northern-ireland.passage: To get Attendance Allowance you must: be habitually resident and in Northern Ireland … You can also call the Disability and Carers Service and ask to be sent a claim pack

hf-affordable.statement: The Health Foundation argues that reform is affordable if the government chooses it.
hf-affordable.passage: But reform is not unaffordable: if it chooses to, government can afford to provide a better, fairer and more generous social care system in England.

hf-broad-estimate.statement: The Health Foundation calls its estimate for universal care a broad estimate.
hf-broad-estimate.passage: This is a broad estimate only.

bsp-30-years.statement: For the full basic State Pension, men born between 1945 and 1951 usually need 30 qualifying years, and men born earlier 44. Women born between 1950 and 1953 usually need 30, and women born earlier 39.
bsp-30-years.passage: If you're a man you usually need: 30 qualifying years if you were born between 1945 and 1951 44 qualifying years if you were born before 1945 If you're a woman you usually need: 30 qualifying years if you were born between 1950 and 1953 39 qualifying years if were born before 1950
bsp-30-years.note: GOV.UK gives the bands by year of birth and by sex.

tl-kept-to-2030.statement: The government says the triple lock stays as it is until April 2030.
tl-kept-to-2030.passage: The current State Pension Triple Lock will be maintained until April 2030.

rule-2030.statement: From April 2030 the government plans a different rule. The State Pension would rise each year by inflation or 2.5%, whichever is higher, and by more if that is needed to keep its value relative to earnings.
rule-2030.passage: From April 2030, the adjusted Triple Lock will mean the State Pension continues to rise by 2.5% or inflation - whichever is higher – and by even more if that is required to maintain its value relative to earnings.
rule-2030.note: An announcement. The rule is not in law. The government has described it in outline, and has not published the measure of earnings or the exact test.

rule-2030-legislate.statement: The government says it will legislate for the change during this Parliament.
rule-2030-legislate.passage: The Government will legislate for the change during this Parliament.

rule-2030-name.statement: The government calls the rule the adjusted triple lock.
rule-2030-name.passage: Savings under the adjusted Triple Lock will be used for a new National Care Service

rule-2030-example.statement: The government gives an example. If the State Pension is about a third of average earnings in 2030/31, it would rise as average earnings rise.
rule-2030-example.passage: if the value of the State Pension is around a third of average earnings by 2030/31, as average earnings rise, the State Pension will rise in line with that too
rule-2030-example.note: An example in the announcement. It is not a published target.

rule-2030-no-fall.statement: The government says no pension will go down.
rule-2030-no-fall.passage: Nobody's pension will ever go down.

ncs-next-parliament.statement: The government says a National Care Service will be set up in the next Parliament, with free personal care for older people, based on need.
ncs-next-parliament.passage: A National Care Service will be established in the next Parliament, providing free personal care for older people, based on need rather than ability to pay.

ncs-personal-care.statement: Personal care means help with things like eating, bathing and using the toilet.
ncs-personal-care.passage: The new system will include personal care, helping with things like eating, bathing and using the toilet.

ncs-not-bed-board.statement: The service would not cover bed and board. The present means-tested council contributions would stay for those.
ncs-not-bed-board.passage: The service will not cover bed and board, for which existing means-tested council contributions will remain.

ncs-phased.statement: The service would be introduced in phases, growing as the savings from the pension change grow and as staff and providers are built up.
ncs-phased.passage: The new National Care Service will be introduced in phases, so its scope can grow as the savings increase from adjusting the Triple Lock, and as workforce and provider capacity are built up.

ncs-not-borrowing.statement: The government says the service will be fully funded, and not through borrowing.
ncs-not-borrowing.passage: It will be fully funded – and not through borrowing.

ncs-savings-used.statement: The government says the savings from the pension change will be used for the care service. Baroness Casey's commission is to recommend how and when the service is built up.
ncs-savings-used.passage: Savings under the adjusted Triple Lock will be used for a new National Care Service, with Baroness Casey to recommend how and when it is built up.
ncs-savings-used.note: A statement of intent. Nothing in law ties one budget to the other.

pm-speech-2030.statement: In his speech the Prime Minister said the pension would still rise every year by at least prices or 2.5%.
pm-speech-2030.passage: The state pension will continue to rise every year at least by prices or 2.5%.
pm-speech-2030.note: From the speech as published by the Labour Party. GOV.UK carries no transcript.

pm-speech-income-tax.statement: In a speech on 29 September 2026 the Prime Minister said pensioners on low incomes would not be "dragged into paying income tax" in this Parliament. Neither the speech nor the government's news story of that day says who counts as being on a low income, or how it would be done.
pm-speech-income-tax.passage: I can also confirm today our commitment to ensure that the low-income pensioners won't be dragged into paying income tax in this Parliament.
pm-speech-income-tax.note: From the speech as published by the Labour Party. GOV.UK carries no transcript. The GOV.UK news story of 29 September 2026 does not mention Income Tax.

ifs-rule-2030-mechanism.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies describes the rule as the highest of three things each year: inflation, 2.5%, or the amount needed for the pension to keep up with the growth in average earnings since the rule began.
ifs-rule-2030-mechanism.passage: the amount needed to ensure the state pension keeps up with average earnings growth since the introduction of the new policy
ifs-rule-2030-mechanism.note: The Institute's description. The government has described the rule in outline only.

ifs-rule-2030-catch-up.statement: In the Institute's description, after a year in which inflation or 2.5% decides the increase, the pension goes on rising by inflation or 2.5% until the growth in average earnings has caught up with it.
ifs-rule-2030-catch-up.passage: it instead continues to rise by 2.5% (or inflation, if higher than 2.5%) each year until the growth in the state pension is matched by growth in average earnings

ifs-ratchet-removed.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the change removes the permanent ratchet.
ifs-ratchet-removed.passage: It removes the most expensive and unattractive element of the old triple lock which is the permanent ratchet effect.

ifs-smoothed-similar.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says a smoothed earnings link is similar to the announced rule, but without the rise of at least 2.5% every year.
ifs-smoothed-similar.passage: is similar to the new triple lock, but it does not include the condition that the state pension must always rise by at least 2.5% each year

ifs-savings-small-early.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies expects the savings to be fairly small in the first few years.
ifs-savings-small-early.passage: The savings to the Exchequer from this reform are likely to be relatively small in the first few years.

ifs-not-universal-care.statement: The deputy director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies says the change should not be expected to save enough to pay for universal social care in the next Parliament.
ifs-not-universal-care.passage: We should not expect this reform to save enough that it could fund universal social care in the next parliament.
ifs-not-universal-care.note: That is about universal care. The government has announced free personal care, in phases.

ifs-floor-arbitrary.statement: He calls the 2.5% minimum arbitrary and possibly costly.
ifs-floor-arbitrary.passage: the minimum 2.5% increase each year remains an arbitrary and potentially costly part of the system

ifs-real-rise-slower.statement: The deputy director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies says pensions would still rise faster than prices over time, but more slowly than under the triple lock.
ifs-real-rise-slower.passage: state pensions will still rise in real terms over time but more slowly than under the current system

rf-response-2030.statement: The Resolution Foundation welcomed the change, and said that putting the savings into social care helps vulnerable pensioners most.
rf-response-2030.passage: recycling the savings into social care is especially good news for vulnerable pensioners

ncs-england-reported.statement: PA News reported that the care service is for England. The government's announcement names no nation.
ncs-england-reported.passage: creating a NHS-style care service in England

wales-funding-reported.statement: The Secretary of State for Wales was reported as saying that a share of the money would go to Wales, and that the Welsh Government would decide how to use it.
wales-funding-reported.passage: The right proportion of that funding will come to Wales, it will then be up to the government of the day to implement a new national care service.
wales-funding-reported.note: Reported from a television interview. We found no government document that says it.

minister-more-funding.statement: A Cabinet minister was reported as saying the care plans could need more funding.

conservative-response.statement: The Conservative leader said the change would not save enough to pay for a care service for two decades.
conservative-response.passage: it won't generate enough savings to fund a nationalised care system for another two decades

conservative-response-next-day.statement: The next day she was reported as saying that the triple lock is her party's policy and in its draft manifesto, when asked whether she could guarantee it would be in the next one.
conservative-response-next-day.passage: Our current policies are in our draft manifesto. The triple lock is our policy and in our draft manifesto.

libdem-response.statement: The Liberal Democrat leader said care reform cannot wait until after another election and cannot be paid for by the poorest pensioners.
libdem-response.passage: cannot wait until after another election and it can't be funded from the pockets of our poorest pensioners

reform-response.statement: Reform UK says it will keep the triple lock.
reform-response.passage: Reform UK will always protect our pensioners and maintain the triple lock

snp-response.statement: The First Minister of Scotland, who leads the Scottish National Party, called the change a bad idea.
snp-response.passage: I think it's a bad idea.

plaid-response.statement: Plaid Cymru's leader at Westminster responded to the speech. In the report we read she did not state a position on the pension change.
plaid-response.passage: there is clear common ground between Andy Burnham's plans for England and what the Plaid Cymru Welsh Government is already delivering in Wales

green-response.statement: The Green Party leader called the speech half measures. In the report we read he did not state a position on the pension change.

unite-response.statement: The general secretary of the Unite union said pensioners should not be asked to pay before the very rich.
unite-response.passage: Going to the well of pensioners before going for the super rich is wrong.

yougov-rule-2030.statement: In a YouGov online poll of 4,503 adults in Great Britain on 29 September 2026, 48% supported changing the triple lock in 2030 to help fund a care service, 28% opposed it and 25% did not know.
yougov-rule-2030.passage: Connecting the triple lock change with contributing funding to a National Care Service increases support – but not by much, at 48%, while the number opposed remains largely the same at 28%
yougov-rule-2030.note: The 25% who did not know is from the chart data published with the article.

yougov-question.statement: The question described the change as making pensions "only increase by whatever is highest out of inflation or 2.5%". It did not mention the part of the announced rule that keeps the pension's value relative to earnings.
yougov-question.passage: Andy Burnham has announced he plans to change the triple lock in 2030 so that pensions only increase by whatever is highest out of inflation or 2.5%.
yougov-question.note: The second sentence compares the question with the GOV.UK news story of 29 September 2026.

ageuk-response.statement: Age UK said it would wait for the detail before judging the pension change.
ageuk-response.passage: we postpone judgment on the overall impact of their proposed reform until we can scrutinise the detail

hf-response.statement: The Health Foundation said more public money would be needed, and that what the service will include is not yet clear.
hf-response.passage: additional public investment will be needed to deliver a fairer and more universal system

kf-response.statement: The King's Fund said many questions remain about how the reforms would work and what they would cost.
kf-response.passage: Many genuine questions remain about how these reforms will work in practice and how much it will cost.

dwp-2030-baseline.statement: The Department for Work and Pensions published an analysis of the change on the day of the announcement. It measures the savings against keeping the triple lock.
dwp-2030-baseline.passage: Savings estimates are produced by comparing long-run projected State Pension expenditure under the adjusted Triple Lock uprating mechanism with expenditure under the current Triple Lock.

dwp-2030-caution.statement: The department says its figures for 2039 to 2040 and 2049 to 2050 are long-term estimates, and should not be used to work out the saving in any other single year.
dwp-2030-caution.passage: These savings should not be used to then derive further point estimates for savings in an individual year and should instead be relied on for long-term estimates.

dwp-2030-coverage.statement: The department says the rule would apply to the basic State Pension and to the full rate of the new State Pension.
dwp-2030-coverage.passage: From April 2030, the bSP and the full rate of the nSP will rise each year by the highest of:

dwp-triple-lock-coverage-now.statement: The department says the triple lock covers the same two rates now.
dwp-triple-lock-coverage-now.passage: The Triple Lock means the basic State Pension (bSP) and the full rate of the new State Pension (nSP) increase by the highest of:

dwp-2030-other-parts.statement: The department's analysis assumes that the parts of a pre-2016 pension that the triple lock does not cover keep rising with prices.
dwp-2030-other-parts.passage: Components of the pre-2016 State Pension that are not covered by the Triple Lock are assumed to continue to be uprated by CPI.

dwp-2030-poverty.statement: The department projects that, under the new rule, the share of pensioners in Great Britain in relative low income after housing costs would fall.
dwp-2030-poverty.passage: relative pensioner poverty after housing costs under the adjusted Triple Lock is projected to fall from around 14% in 2024 to 2025 to around 8% in 2049 to 2050.

dwp-2030-poverty-conditional.statement: It says this is a projection that depends on its assumptions, not a prediction.
dwp-2030-poverty-conditional.passage: Results are projections conditional on the assumptions used, rather than predictions of future poverty rates.

dwp-2030-poverty-not-effect.statement: The projection is measured against 2024 to 2025, not against keeping the triple lock, so it does not show what the change itself does to poverty.
dwp-2030-poverty-not-effect.passage: Chart 1: Projected changes in pensioner relative poverty after housing costs compared to 2024 to 2025
dwp-2030-poverty-not-effect.note: Our reading of the chart's title and the method, which compares incomes with a poverty line, not with the triple lock.

no-rule-2030-detail.statement: We found no Bill for the change to the triple lock. The government has not published the measure of earnings the rule would use, or the paths of earnings and prices behind its savings estimates.
no-rule-2030-detail.note: Searched on 5 October 2026: GOV.UK, the announcement, the Department for Work and Pensions' analysis of 29 September 2026, and the UK Parliament's list of Bills. A search on 30 September 2026 missed that analysis. Searched again on 8 October 2026: GOV.UK publications and news since 5 October 2026 for "triple lock", "national care service", "state pension uprating" and "adult social care commission", which found only the department's factsheet of 6 October 2026; and the UK Parliament's list of Bills for "triple lock", "state pension", "pension" and "uprating".

no-rule-2030-distribution.statement: We found no published analysis of who would gain and who would lose from the pension change and the care service together.
no-rule-2030-distribution.note: Searched on 30 September 2026: GOV.UK, the Institute for Fiscal Studies and the Resolution Foundation. Both bodies give totals, not effects on groups of people.

no-ncs-nations.statement: The government's announcement does not say which nations the care service covers, or how pensioners in the other nations would be treated.
no-ncs-nations.note: A reading of the whole GOV.UK news story of 29 September 2026. News reports say the service is for England, and one reports a minister saying money would go to Wales.

no-ncs-cost.statement: We found no government estimate of what the care service would cost.
no-ncs-cost.note: Searched on 30 September 2026: the GOV.UK news story and news reports. Reports give figures without naming a source.

no-rule-2030-pension-credit.statement: We found nothing on what the change means for Pension Credit.
no-rule-2030-pension-credit.note: Searched on 30 September 2026: the GOV.UK news story, the speech as printed, and the two Institute for Fiscal Studies pieces. Searched again on 8 October 2026: the department's analysis and its factsheet of 6 October 2026.

ifs-rule-2030-illustration.statement: The Institute for Fiscal Studies gives an example over ten years. Prices rise by 2% every year. Earnings rise by 4% a year, except for three years at 1%. In those three years the pension rises by 2.5%. When earnings growth recovers, the pension goes on rising by 2.5% until earnings have caught up. Then it follows earnings again.
ifs-rule-2030-illustration.passage: By year 9, the growth in the state pension has matched the growth in average earnings since year 1, and so the state pension returns to rising in line with average earnings growth.
ifs-rule-2030-illustration.note: A stylised example by the Institute, not a forecast. Under the triple lock in the same example the pension follows earnings again at once, and stays permanently higher.

rule-2030-needs-law.statement: In a year when the pension is waiting for earnings to catch up, the announced rule would pay less than that year's earnings growth. The present law does not allow that, so the law would have to change.
rule-2030-needs-law.passage: under the new triple lock the state pension does not grow in line with earnings
rule-2030-needs-law.note: Our reading. It joins the Institute's description of the rule to the legal minimum described on the triple lock page.

press-double-lock.statement: Some news reports call the announced rule a double lock.
press-double-lock.passage: the state pension will become a double lock

ncs-home-deferred.statement: Councils would still leave out the value of a home where a partner or dependent relative lives there, and deferred payment agreements would stay.
ncs-home-deferred.passage: Councils will continue to exclude the value of a home from financial assessments where a partner or dependent relative lives there, and deferred payment agreements will remain available

spa-born-before-1960.statement: Everyone born before 6 April 1960 has reached State Pension age. The last to do so were born between 6 October 1954 and 5 April 1960, and reached it at 66.
spa-born-before-1960.note: Our reading of the timetable. People born on 5 April 1960 reached 66 on 5 April 2026.

spa-born-1960-61.statement: People born between 6 April 1960 and 5 March 1961 reach State Pension age at 66 and between 1 and 11 months, depending on their month of birth.
spa-born-1960-61.passage: people born between 6 April 1960 and 5 March 1961 will reach their State Pension age at 66 years and the specified number of months

spa-born-1961-77.statement: For people born between 6 March 1961 and 5 April 1977, State Pension age is 67.

spa-born-1977-78.statement: For people born between 6 April 1977 and 5 April 1978, State Pension age falls between 67 and 68. The law sets a date for each month of birth, from 6 May 2044 to 6 March 2046.
spa-born-1977-78.note: Table 5 of the timetable gives the date for each month of birth.

spa-born-from-1978.statement: For people born on or after 6 April 1978, State Pension age is 68.

spa-68-review.statement: The timetable for the rise from 67 to 68 could change as a result of a review.
spa-68-review.passage: the timetable for the increase in the State Pension age from 67 to 68 could change as a result of the review
